restrictions: Target blake3-r7-prefix-v1 exactly: unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with prefix rounds 0..6 in every chunk, parent and root compression, standard IV, standard message permutation, full 256-bit output as the first 32 little-endian root output bytes.

Both colliding messages are complete 32-byte inputs, so each hash is one chunk compression (CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END, counter 0) followed by the root compression (ROOT). No free-start, compression-only or truncated-output collision is claimed.

The attack is generic: parallel collision search (van Oorschot-Wiener) on h(x) = blake3-r7(x). The declared work is the expected search length sqrt(pi*N/2) = 1.2533 x 2^128 evaluations for N = 2^256, with the 0.39 success probability floor; no cryptanalytic weakness of BLAKE3 or of its 7-round prefix is asserted, and improvesNominalReference is false by construction.

Accounting: each evaluation is one target compression; six word primitives per evaluation (digest-word load, distinguished-point mask test, comparison, branch, counter) are charged at 6/1470 units with the BLAKE3 r7 reference operation cost 1470 extrapolated from the organizer's r1 = 222 and r2 = 430 (208 per additional round). Total 2^128.3256 x 1.00408 = 2^128.3315, declared 128.34 (rounded up). At C = 222 the same bookkeeping gives 128.36; the sensitivity is declared in proof Section 7.

Preprocessing and advice are zero rather than omitted: the search starts from fresh random start values with no precomputed table, no stored distinguished-point database and no nonuniform advice. Every evaluation of every walk, including walks discarded as rho cycles, lies inside the declared expectation.

Memory is 2^20 bytes exactly: 2^14 distinguished-point records of 32 bytes (2^19) sorted in place, plus program code, working state and one replay path bounded by 2^19. No digest table is retained. Under hashsmash-scalar-tm-v1 the memory term is log2(2^20 / 2^20) = 0.

This row sets the generic cost at the top of the admitted round range 3..7 so that later cryptanalytic rows can be compared against it. It is not a certificate: no colliding pair is exhibited, because exhibiting one would cost the declared 2^128 evaluations.

heuristics.statement: Parallel collision search on a random 256-bit function finds a collision in expected sqrt(pi*N/2) = 1.2533 x 2^128 evaluations with N = 2^256, and q = 2^128 distinct evaluations already yield a collision with probability 1 - exp(-q^2/2N) = 0.3935, above the declared 0.39.
heuristics.scope: The iteration function h(x) = blake3-r7(x) on 32-byte values, modelled as a random function from {0,1}^256 to {0,1}^256. The 1.2533 constant covers walk restarts and the rho-cycle discard and replay treatment.
heuristics.extrapolation: Van Oorschot and Wiener, Parallel Collision Search with Cryptanalytic Applications, Journal of Cryptology 12(1), 1999: the expected number of evaluations with a distinguished-point memo is sqrt(pi*N/2) up to a factor 1 + O(2^-w) in the distinguished-point width w, with w = 113 here.
heuristics.limitations: The constant is an expectation, not a high-probability bound; a reviewer who prices a 0.9-probability search instead would raise the declared time by about 0.4 bit. The 0.39 floor is declared at the q = 2^128 birthday point, which is conservative relative to the expected work charged.

heuristics.statement: The whole working set is 2^20 bytes: 2^14 distinguished-point records of 32 bytes sorted in place, plus code, state and one replay path bounded by 2^19 bytes; no digest table is retained and no memory is retained across restarts beyond the sorted memo.
heuristics.scope: The online search program only. There is no preprocessing phase and therefore no preprocessing memory.
heuristics.extrapolation: Memory accounting of the shipped search loop; the distinguished-point width 2^-113 sets the number of records (2^14) for a 2^128-evaluation search.
heuristics.limitations: Code size is bounded rather than measured byte for byte; the bound 2^19 leaves 100 percent headroom over a compiled search loop of a few hundred instructions with a 512 KiB sorted memo.

heuristics.statement: Preprocessing and nonuniform advice are exactly zero: the search begins from fresh random 32-byte start values with no precomputed table, no stored collision, no distinguished-point database and no advice derived from any prior run.
heuristics.scope: Every input to the search program: its code, its random coins and the target profile.
heuristics.extrapolation: The program's only state before the first evaluation is its own code and the fresh random start values; nothing about the target is precomputed, so there is no omitted search to charge.
heuristics.limitations: If a reviewer holds that the generic birthday bound for a standard hash embeds a preprocessing assumption, the correct charge is 0 anyway: the bound is information-theoretic in the digest width, not in any table.
